verdict.left_looks: A flat-roofed rectangular box with a checkerboard black/white base course, tall black pillars between large glass-pane bays with light-blue frames, and a gray/tan flat parapet band on top. The interior is visible: hay bales, wooden barrels/counters, a wooden door in the centre, and a few potted plants. It's a glass-fronted shop or cafe. There is no site base, and the form is repetitive and rigid. The back is the same glass-and-pillar rhythm.
verdict.right_looks: A compact black-walled building on a stone-brick plinth, with a large overhanging roof slab of oak planks, a black band and a dark cap. The front has a small double wooden door, a few small windows, an orange awning/sign block, a glowstone sign, lanterns, leaf-bush planters, and small tables. The sides are mostly blank black walls with a couple of windows, and the back is a large featureless black wall. It reads as a small cafe or shop on a terrace.
verdict.why: The right build has a layered silhouette (plinth, overhanging roof) plus entrance, lanterns, planters and signage that give it character and street presence, while the left is a repetitive glass box with no roof or site treatment, even though its glazing and interior are well done.
